decidedBy: the project owner, 2026-11-01, of the report on PRB-1417: 'Да, виправ це все'; each record read against its verses by claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-01
policy: Where a place of one name may be another of that name, both pages say so. Where a word stands on the wrong one of two, the verse says which.
source: Essenthos, places of one name read against their verses by claude-opus-5-5 on the project owner's word of 2026-11-01

alternatives.reason: Jeremiah's Migdol in Egypt (JER 44:1; 46:14) may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Migdol by which Israel camped (EXO 14:2) may be this one; the text does not say.

alternatives.reason: The tower of Ezekiel's prophecy against Egypt, in the Hebrew Migdol (EZK 29:10; 30:6), may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Migdol by which Israel camped (EXO 14:2) may be this one; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Between Migdol and the sea' (EXO 14:2): the camp before the crossing. All three Migdol records are put at Tell el Herr among other sites; the text does not join them.

alternatives.reason: The tower of Ezekiel's prophecy against Egypt, in the Hebrew Migdol (EZK 29:10; 30:6), may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: Jeremiah's Migdol in Egypt (JER 44:1; 46:14) may be this one; the text does not say.

rulings.why: Jeremiah's Migdol, in the land of Egypt; Ezekiel's 'from Migdol to Syene' may be the same town.

alternatives.reason: The Ramah of Benjamin (JOS 18:25) may be Samuel's town; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: Samuel's Ramah (1SA 1:19; 7:17) may be this town; the text does not say.

rulings.why: Samuel's Ramah: the gazetteer gives it as another name for Ramah of Benjamin, and also at Beit Rima. The text does not say.

alternatives.reason: The sea Israel crossed (EXO 15:4) may be this one; the text calls both the Red Sea.
alternatives.back: The Red Sea of the locusts and of the camp after Elim (EXO 10:19; NUM 33:10) may be this sea; the text calls both the Red Sea.

alternatives.reason: The Red Sea by Ezion-geber in Edom (1KI 9:26) may be this one; the text calls both the Red Sea.
alternatives.back: The Red Sea of the locusts and of the camp after Elim (EXO 10:19; NUM 33:10) may be this sea; the text calls both the Red Sea.

rulings.why: The Red sea of the locusts (EXO 10:19), the gazetteer's Red Sea 3: at the Gulf of Suez, 'another name for Red Sea 1', and also at the Gulf of Aqaba.
'The way of the wilderness of the Red sea' (EXO 13:18), the road to the crossing.

alternatives.reason: The Hazazon-tamar of 2 Chronicles, which is En-gedi (2CH 20:2), may be this one; Genesis does not say.
alternatives.back: The Hazazon-tamar where the Amorites dwelt (GEN 14:7) may be this one; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 2CH 20:2 says its Hazazontamar is En-gedi. Whether Genesis's is that one the text does not say; the gazetteer also gives Tamar and Wadi Hasasah.

alternatives.reason: The place behind Kirjath-jearim called Mahaneh-dan (JDG 18:12) may be this camp; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol (JDG 13:25) may be this place; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'The camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol' (JDG 13:25). The verse names this camp, not the place behind Kirjath-jearim of JDG 18:12.

alternatives.reason: The Levites' Jokmeam (1CH 6:68) may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Jokmeam of Solomon's district (1KI 4:12) may be this one; the text does not say.

alternatives.reason: The King James prints Jokneam at this verse, and Jokneam by Carmel (JOS 12:22) may be this place; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Jokmeam the Hebrew writes at 1KI 4:12, where the King James prints Jokneam, may be this place; the text does not say.

rulings.why: Baana's district reaches the place 'beyond Jokneam' (KJV), in the Hebrew Jokmeam. The verse names the place of the district; whether that is the Levites' Jokmeam or Jokneam by Carmel the text does not say.
'Kir of Moab' (ISA 15:1): the Moabite town, not the land Assyria carried Damascus to.

alternatives.reason: Bethsaida of Galilee, the city of Philip, Andrew and Peter (JHN 1:44; 12:21), may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Bethsaida the disciples crossed to (MRK 6:45; 8:22) may be this one; the text does not say.

rulings.why: The gazetteer sets Bethsaida in Galilee (JHN 12:21) beside Bethsaida in Gaulanitis, and gives the second as another name for the first. Mark 6:45 sends the disciples across to a Bethsaida from near the Bethsaida of LUK 9:10, which is why two have been proposed. The text does not settle it, so the two stay apart with the question on both.
Amaziah's Selah, called Joktheel (2KI 14:7), the gazetteer's Sela 2.

alternatives.reason: The Selah that Amaziah took and called Joktheel (2KI 14:7) may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Sela of Isaiah's word on Moab (ISA 16:1) may be this one; the text does not say.

rulings.why: The gazetteer's Sela 3, of ISA 16:1, 'may be a different, unknown location farther north'. So not folded with Amaziah's Selah; the question is on both.

alternatives.reason: The Tamar the Hebrew writes at 1KI 9:18, among the towns Solomon built, may be this one; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Tamar of Ezekiel's southern border (EZK 47:19) may be this one; the text does not say.

rulings.why: The Hebrew of 1KI 9:18 writes Tamar where 2CH 8:4 and the King James have Tadmor. The gazetteer gives both, Tamar 2 and Tadmor. So not folded; the question is on both.

alternatives.reason: The Hebrew writes Tamar at this verse where the King James and 2CH 8:4 have Tadmor, so the town may be another Tamar; the text does not say.
alternatives.back: The Tadmor of 2CH 8:4, which the King James prints at 1KI 9:18 too, may be this town; the text does not say.

rulings.why: The word stays on Tadmor, whose number it carries and as the King James prints it; the other reading is said on both pages.
'Of the sons of Nebo' (EZR 10:43): a family's forefather, whose record the list of Ezra 2 already names, not the town.
